wake.description: a scheduled time to come back to something
wake.$comment: A wake carries no patch to apply when it fires: a rule's produce already writes the entity it matched. Patching a wake's target declaratively would need a rule that names that target.

at.description: when it is next due; absent once a one-shot has fired, or once a recurrence has ended

target.description: what the wake is about; when absent, the entity carrying it

note.description: a line for whoever is woken: why the wake was set

every.description: how it recurs: a duration (30m, 2h, 1d), five cron fields (0 9 * * 1-5), or @hourly/@daily/@weekly/@monthly; a cron line may end with an IANA time zone (0 9 * * 1-5 America/New_York), otherwise UTC

while.description: how it recurs while something holds: {match, every} in order, a query over the whole store and the cadence it asks for; at each firing the first whose query finds anything sets the next instant, else every does, and with neither the wake sleeps until a write makes one hold

match.description: holds while this query finds anything

every.description: the cadence while it holds, written as wake.every is

for.description: the person it was set for: it runs as them, with their permissions as they stand when it fires, and it is theirs to list and cancel

brief.description: words for a fresh session started at each firing, given the outcome of the call it carries: a helper that checks the work and tells whom it is for only when they should hear

wake_new.title: Schedule a wake
wake_new.description: Come back to something later: once at an instant, or on a cadence. Each firing knocks whoever attends the target with the note: a persona's operator, or the session opened on a topic (a goal or project that is its own topic). Returns the wake.

target.description: What the wake is about: a persona, a topic, a goal or project id.

every.description: How it recurs: a duration (30m, 1d), five cron fields with an optional time zone (0 7 * * * America/Detroit), or @hourly/@daily/@weekly/@monthly.

at.description: When it is next due: an instant (2026-01-02T09:00Z), or a delay from now (10m, 2h, 1d). With every, the first firing. Without every, it fires once.

note.description: A line for whoever is woken: what to do.

wake_list.title: List your wakes
wake_list.description: The wakes set for you that will fire again, soonest first: each one's id, when it next fires, how it recurs, its note, the query it watches, the call it makes and when it last fired.

wake_cancel.title: Cancel a wake
wake_cancel.description: Cancel a wake set for you, by its id, so it never fires again. Returns the wake cancelled.

wake.description: The wake's id, as wake_new or wake_list gave it.

watch.description: a query a wake watches: each time the wake comes due its rows are read again, and it fires only when they changed since it last looked; a look that finds nothing new moves it on without firing

query.description: the query whose rows it watches, written as for graph_query

local.description: read over the store the wake is kept in, rather than everything its person reaches (on yaks.app, the space's apps)

seen.description: each row the query answered at the last look, by eid, and a digest of what it held

changes.description: what changed at the look the wake last fired for, in words: rows new, changed and gone

occurrence.description: one firing of a wake that did work; completed or failed says how it ended

wake.description: the wake that fired, kept when it is cancelled

call.description: the call it made, whose answer is that call's own record (@yaks/tools)

error.description: the call's failure, kept while a session given the wake's brief checks its outcome

wake_run.description: Do what a wake set for a person asks each time it fires: its call with no model turn (an occurrence records it), its note in their conversation, and its brief to a fresh session. The host that runs sessions handles it; owed only where @yaks/wake is given run: true

wake.description: a scheduled time to come back to something
